question_text: Fill in: 'The employee was commended ___ her outstanding performance.'

hint_ladder.title: Think about the verb
hint_ladder.text: 'Commended' means praised. How do we usually link praise to its reason? Think: 'praised for her hard work.'

hint_ladder.title: The reason rule
hint_ladder.text: To state the reason for praise, 'for' is the go-to preposition. Like 'thank you for' your help.

hint_ladder.title: Test each option
hint_ladder.text: Say it aloud: 'commended with' means with something else; 'commended about' is for topics; 'commended on' is for areas. Only 'for' gives the reason.

hint_ladder.title: Narrow it down
hint_ladder.text: 'On' might seem okay for specific skills, but here performance is the reason. Stick with 'for' every time you state a cause.

A.text: Correct. 'Commended for' is the standard pairing to give the reason for praise.

B.text: You might have chosen B because you thought of being praised along with a reward, but the sentence calls for the reason, not accompaniment.

C.text: You might have chosen C because you know 'talk about,' but 'commended about' isn't standard English; it doesn't state a reason.

D.text: You might have chosen D because 'on' can point to an area, but 'outstanding performance' is the reason, so 'for' is correct.

next_time_rule: For reasons after 'commended,' always choose 'for.' Remember: praised FOR a reason, not ON a reason. It's the safest choice.
deconstruct_text:
Let's break this down. The employee was commended — praised — because of her performance. That performance is the reason. In English, after 'commended,' the preposition 'for' is the natural choice to link to that reason. It's like saying 'thanked for' — same logic.

Imagine a local scenario: Barangay Secretary Maria is commended for her exceptional work in disaster aid. Everyone understands she's praised because of that work. That's exactly how 'for' functions here — it points to the reason.

**Watch-Out Zone: preposition_misuse** in action. 'With' is for accompaniment, 'on' for...

Mental trick: 'Commended FOR' = dahilan, 'siya ay pinuri dahil sa galing.' Next time, isipin mo 'for reason' — lagyan mo ng arrow pababa, 'for' agad. That's the simple rule to never second-guess.
